entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: What did you ask me here to discuss?

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: ...I heard you met with[n]Kuramoto's grandson.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: You have your ears to the ground, huh?

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: And to think that he's the candidate[n]the party is backing to ruin my chances[n]of winning...

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I'll be completely straight with you,[n]since I already asked you to be my[n]right-hand man.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: We're currently fighting the[n]Kuramoto group.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: You're fighting with Mr. Kuramoto!?

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I have ambitions of my own, you know.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I owe him for all he did for me,[n]but I don't want him to have[n]influence over me forever.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: All the more, now that he's[n]secretly working with Diet[n]members from other parties.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: All the more, now that he's secretly[n]working with Shido's Diet members.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I know he asked you to join his group,[n]but I think you should decline his offer.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: They want to keep you on a leash, so you[n]won't reveal any damaging information.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: The real culprit of the expense[n]misappropriation case you were[n]blamed for... is old man Kuramoto.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: What did you say...!?

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I searched through the party's off-[n]the-record accounts from twenty[n]years ago. There's no doubt.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: Can you still forgive him? He led[n]you into the political world and[n]kicked you out in the worst way!

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: But why...?

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: Seems he bought his popularity,[n]and as a result, he was having[n]some serious financial trouble.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: It sounds as if you're saying that this is[n]my opportunity to clear my name...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: ...And so you need an answer from[n]me on whether or not I'll be your[n]right-hand man, yes?

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: His own grandson has already[n]tried to persuade you. Therefore,[n]I can't wait any longer.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: If you join me, you can accuse[n]Kuramoto of his crime.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: You can clear your name and put[n]No-Good Tora behind you. This is[n]your best and last chance!

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Join with Matsushita and take[n]my revenge against Mr. Kuramoto,[n]but drop out of the election...
Are you going to do it?
Don't do it.
That's a difficult decision.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: It's a good deal, if I think[n]about the future. However...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: I see... so that's how you[n]truly feel about this...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Yes, to say the least...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: ...Matsushita.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: I appreciate the offer, but I must refuse.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: You have no conceivable[n]REASON to refuse!

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: My goal is to become a member of[n]the Diet, not a right-hand man. [n]I will not cast aside my beliefs.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: On that I stand firm.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: This information would be[n]the deciding factor in[n]taking down Kuramoto...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: I'm sorry.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: Don't worry about it. I was simply[n]offering you a deal. I assumed you[n]might decline it...

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: ...Very well. Please forget it. I apologize[n]for bringing it up so suddenly.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I'll talk to the party and provide[n]support for your next speech[n]about the Phantom Thieves.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Why are you doing this?

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: I don't want a debate about[n]the Phantom Thieves. I simply[n]want to draw attention to them.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: And you can assert your innocence[n]there, on a grand stage.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: To be frank, I'll be happy as long as the[n]Kuramoto group's influence diminishes.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: [lName]-kun... Don't speak a[n]word of this to anyone, for[n]both our sakes.

entries.speaker: Dietman Matsushita
entries.en: Very well, then.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: It feels like I'm caught in the[n]crossfire of a political conspiracy.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: My friend is trying to take advantage[n]of me, while my former mentor is[n]trying to win me over.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: To achieve my dream, I have to set aside[n]my beliefs. What should I do?
Stick to your beliefs.[clr 27]
Clear your name.
Get elected.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: You're right. Betraying myself[n]means betraying my supporters.[n]Which also means betraying you.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: People go back on their words[n]all the time in the political[n]world. It's quite risky.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Indeed, this would all be futile if[n]I don't become a Diet member.[n]I must focus on getting elected.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: However, betraying oneself to reach[n]a goal would be a hollow victory indeed.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: For some reason, just talking with you[n]always helps me make up my mind.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: It's as if my heart is being manipulated.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Perhaps...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: If the Phantom Thieves truly do exist...[n]then I'm sure they're very much like you.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: For some reason you stood by me,[n]No-Good Tora, who didn't have[n]any supporters.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: I've been thinking about this[n]for a while, actually.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: You must've experienced cruelty and[n]injustice in this life. I can tell by the[n]look in your eyes.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: That's why I sense your[n]desire to help the weak.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: And the strength to stand up to[n]the hecklers, to Matsushita, and[n]to Kuramoto's grandson.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: You're no ordinary high school student.[n]Even I know that much.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Would you care to... talk about it?
What good would that do?
So what if you're right?

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: ...Just a joke.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Haha, sorry. I crossed the line there.[n]I've always lacked restraint in these[n]situations...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: See what I did there? I relieved[n]the tension by making fun of myself.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Think of it as an advanced technique[n]for winning people over.
I feel like my bond with[n]Yoshida is growing deeper...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: All right then...

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Well, I'll at least make good use[n]of Matsushita's help setting up[n]my next speech.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: I feel like I'll be able to fully express[n]my beliefs if you're there with me.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: We can discuss it again at the speech.

entries.speaker: Yoshida
entries.en: Good work today.
